examples.text: The elusive criminal was arrested

glosses: Difficult to make precise.

glosses: Rarely seen.

examples.text: While you're sniffing the trunks of the ponderosas to see if they're butterscotch, vanilla, strawberry, or the elusive chocolate variety, watch for Brown Creepers, an elusive variety of bird.

glosses: A person who flees or escapes and travels secretly from place to place, and sometimes using disguises and aliases to conceal their identity, as to avoid law authorities in order to avoid an arrest or prosecution, or to avoid some other unwanted situation.

examples.text: “I don't mean all of your friends—only a small proportion—which, however, connects your circle with that deadly, idle, brainless bunch—the insolent chatterers at the opera,[…]the speed-mad fugitives from the furies of ennui, the neurotic victims of mental cirrhosis, the jewelled animals whose moral code is the code of the barnyard—!”

glosses: Fleeing or running away; escaping.

examples.text: I found afterwards that he was the chauffeur, who filled the gaps left by a succession of fugitive butlers.

glosses: Transient, fleeting or ephemeral.
Elusive or difficult to retain.
To render someone a fugitive; to drive into escape or exile.

examples.text: Her son Thomas was fugitived in the persecution.

glosses: Que l’on ne peut saisir valablement.

examples.text: Certains objets sont déclarés insaisissables par la loi : Une pension insaisissable ou une rente viagère stipulée insaisissable.

glosses: Dont on ne parvient pas à s’emparer.

examples.text: Les fells rôdaient, insaisissables ; on les croyait ici, ils apparaissaient plus loin ; on partait les y chercher, ils se trouvaient ailleurs.

glosses: Qui ne peut être saisi par l’esprit.

examples.text: J’avoue que, pour moi, cette différence est tout à fait insaisissable.

glosses: Qualifie une personne si occupée, si affairée que l’on ne peut avoir un entretien avec elle ni même la rencontrer.
That which cannot be precisely defined or put into words.

examples.text: They apparently have a theory that the indefinable psychic gift that they call magic, and which we might designate "psychicism", can be acquired by accosting the soul of a murdered man in a burial ground at midnight.

glosses: That which defies description; indescribable.
Anything that cannot be defined.
Impossible (or very difficult) to describe.

examples.text: He proved it with indescribable mathematics.

Presently the men set up the melancholy little chant that I had heard on the first night when we were captured in the whaleboat, and the effect produced by their voices was very curious, and quite indescribable.

But there was also about him an indescribable air which no mechanic could have acquired in the practice of his handicraft however dishonestly exercised: [...] the air of moral nihilism common to keepers of gambling hells and disorderly houses; [...]

glosses: Exceeding all description.

examples.text: Our hotel had an indescribable view of the Bay of Naples.

The time was when, had such an idea entered her mind, it would have been torture indescribable and agony the most intense; but then, subdued as was the usual warmth of her temperament, an awful suspension seemed to hold her feelings in control.

glosses: Incapable of being perceived by the senses; incorporeal.
Anything intangible.

examples.text: Diaghilev's love for Nijinsky was as deep and as sincere and reliant as a bond could be, it being based on all those intangibles of love that cannot be enumerated.

glosses: Incorporeal property that is saleable though not material, such as bank deposits, stocks, bonds, and promissory notes.
Unable to be reached; impossible to attain.

examples.text: […] read-only attribute that lists the unreachable but uncollectable objects.

glosses: A person or thing that cannot be reached.

examples.text: “Brands want to be in front of this audience,” Ms. Bamford said. “Reaching these unreachables, these cord-cutters who don’t want to be fed an ad, is a huge concern.”
